# Getting started with Podio API

### What is the Podio API?

The Podio API is a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality. We currently provide wrappers for [PHP](https://github.com/podio-community/podio-php), [.NET](https://developers.podio.com/clients/dotnet), [Ruby](https://developers.podio.com/clients/ruby), [Java](https://developers.podio.com/clients/java), [Python](https://developers.podio.com/clients/python), [Android](http://podio.github.io/podio-android/) and [Objective-C](http://podio.github.io/podio-objc/) which make working with common API operations very simple.

### What can you do with it?

Quite a lot! In fact, the entire Podio frontend is built on the API, and we've exposed it all for you to use too. If you want to build event-driven applications, you have the ability to register [webhooks](https://developers.podio.com/examples/webhooks) in your Podio apps. There are some sensible [rate-limits](https://developers.podio.com/index/limits) in place, but if you need us to raise them for your app, get in touch.

### How do I get started?

You'll need a Podio account, first of all. Then you should review [our Terms of API use](https://api.sharefile.com/home/tos) and then [grab an API key](https://developers.podio.com/api-key) for each app you want to build from your account settings page.

We recommend that you start out by getting to know the [concepts and conventions](https://developers.podio.com/index/overview) of Podio and its API and learn how to [authenticate](https://developers.podio.com/authentication) with us, before you dive into the [tutorials](https://developers.podio.com/examples) and the [documentation](https://developers.podio.com/doc).

You will probably also want to look at our [client libraries](https://developers.podio.com/clients) to see if we have one available for your prefered language or platform.

If you need a hand, please post in the [API developer forum](https://support.sharefile.com/s/question/0D5Dn00001OYmgjKAD/the-api-developer-forum-is-changing-home).
